problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -4 \\ -1 & 2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

The matrix above has eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=1,$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-3.$ Find a Jordan canonical form of the matrix.

The matrix above has eigenvalues $\lambda_1=8,$ $\lambda_2=7,$ and $\lambda_3=4.$ Find a Jordan canonical form of the matrix.
examples.worked_solution:
Notice that we are given a $3 \times 3$ matrix that has precisely $3$ distinct eigenvalues. 

Therefore, $A$ is diagonalizable, and its Jordan canonical form is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14073225/assets/79bf6b6c00e76745d278dcc75e8105447d31074ad42f998f684e66b3929178aa.png)
